Hi!

So people are born with different intelligence, right? If the answer to that question is yes, at what age do people diverge intelligence wise?

What I mean by that is, if John will grow up to have an IQ of 80 and Fred will grow up to have an IQ of 100, what IQ will both people have when they're 5, 10, and 15?

Will they both share similar IQ levels up to a certain age and *then* diverge, or would John have a lower IQ than Fred even at a very young age?

PS: I'm aware there are other methods to determine intelligence other than IQ, but I used that for practicality's sake.
At what age do people diverge, intelligence wise?

I'm not an expert, nor did I google anything. I just have some experience with IQ test.

I was tested when I was ten, and I got a score of 140 +/- and a second time when I was 17 and got a score of 135. The second time I was sleep deprived and on the verge of a mental breakdown. So with that in mind I would say that my IQ has been pretty constant for the biggest part of my life.

The testing gets a bit skewed by the fact that the tests rely on the individual being tested understanding what is being asked well enough to respond in a way that indicates they are intelligent.

At a young age you don't get much of that, so if you are going to try to identify when the results diverge, it is going to be the same point that the individuals being tested start to understand the questions.

If you are asking generically about intelligence I think, and there is some decent science to support, that potential intelligence is effectively static to a particular individual. There is a ton of disagreement about how much of it is genetic. There are things you can have happen that prevent an individual from reaching their potential, but to some degree the differences are there throughout.

IQ testing actively tries to offset the differences in age / learning / background to get at this underlying concept, but by its very nature it is an imperfect attempt.
